Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 86, verses 5–9:

﴿So let man look at what he was created from﴾. That is, from what thing his Lord created him. That is, let him look with the look of one who reflects.

Then He explained, saying: ﴿He was created from a gushing fluid﴾, that is, poured out into the womb. This is the semen (al-mani). It is an active participle (fa'il) with the meaning of a passive (maf'ul), like His saying "a pleasing life" [al-Haqqah: 21], meaning "a pleasing one." Al-daf' means pouring. He meant the water of the man and the water of the woman, because the child is created from both of them, and He made it singular because they are mixed together.

﴿It comes out from between the backbone and the ribs﴾, meaning the backbone of the man and the ribs of the woman. "Al-tara'ib" is the plural of al-tariba, which are the bones of the chest and the upper chest. Ibn Abbas said: they are the place of the necklace on the chest. Al-Walibi related from him: between the woman's breasts. Qatadah said: the upper chest. Ibn Zayd said: the chest.

﴿Indeed He is able to return him﴾. Mujahid said: to return the drop into the urethra. Ikrimah said: to return the water into the backbone from which it came out. Al-Dahhak said: indeed He is able to return man to water as he was before. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: [if He wills, He returns him] [[In "B": "If you wish, I would return him."]] from old age to youth, from youth to childhood, and from childhood to the drop. Ibn Zayd said: indeed He is able to hold back that water so that it does not come out. Qatadah said: indeed Allah is able to resurrect man and bring him back. This is the best of these opinions, because of His saying: ﴿On the day when the secrets are tested﴾.

﴿On the day when the secrets are tested﴾. That is the Day of Resurrection, when the secrets are tested, and hidden things are made manifest. Qatadah and Muqatil said: the deeds are tested. [[In "B": "If you wish, I would return him."]] Ata ibn Abi Rabah said: the secrets are the obligatory acts, such as fasting, prayer, ablution, and the ritual bath after sexual impurity, for they are secrets between Allah the Exalted and the servant. So if the servant wished, he would say, "I fasted," when he had not fasted, or "I prayed," when he had not prayed, or "I performed the ritual bath," when he had not performed it. Therefore he is tested until it becomes clear who performed them from among those who neglected them.

Ibn Umar said: On the Day of Resurrection, every secret will be in the hands of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so it will be an adornment on some faces and a disgrace on other faces. That is: whoever performed them, his face will be bright, and whoever neglected them, his face will be dusty.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 86, verse 10–17:

﴿So he will have no power and no helper.﴾ That is, this human being who denies the Resurrection has no power by which he can protect himself from the punishment of Allah, and no helper who can defend him from Allah.

Then He mentioned another oath, saying: ﴿By the sky, the one with returning rain,﴾ that is, the one with rain, because it returns every year and recurs. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the cloud, which returns with rain.

﴿And by the earth, the one that splits open,﴾ that is, it splits open and cracks to bring forth plants, trees and rivers.

The answer to the oath is His saying: ﴿Indeed, it﴾ meaning the Qur'an ﴿is a decisive word,﴾ a true and serious statement that distinguishes between truth and falsehood.

﴿And it is not a jest,﴾ not play and falsehood.

Then He informed about the polytheists of Makkah, saying: ﴿Indeed, they are plotting a plot,﴾ they fear the Prophet (ﷺ) and show what is contrary to what they really hold.

﴿And I am plotting a plot.﴾ The plot of Allah is His gradually leading them on from where they do not know.

﴿So give the disbelievers respite;﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: this is a threat from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, against them. ﴿Give them a little time,﴾ a little while. The meaning of (mahhil) and (amhil) is: wait and do not hasten. So Allah seized them on the Day of Badr, and the granting of respite was abrogated (nusikha) by the verse of the sword.
